clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female with a history of excessive alcohol consumption presented with dizziness, unsteady gait, recurrent falls, and ataxic gait. Initial CT scan showed chronic small vessel disease and mild cerebral atrophy but no acute pathology. Subsequent MRI revealed FLAIR hyperintensity in the corpus callosum splenium and fornix, and pericallosal white matter hyperintensity. A neuro-radiology meeting concluded these findings, including marked cerebellar atrophy, were consistent with Marchiafava-Bignami Disease (MBD). Management included vitamin B supplementation, alcohol cessation advice, and physiotherapy.
